# VibeRaven

VibeRaven gives AI-built apps production context and checks across Supabase, Vercel, Stripe and the other providers they use, read from the repo, locally, before launch and after a change.

## Two users at once

`race` tests your app’s database on real PostgreSQL 18.6, without Docker, and replays exactly what broke. Start locally with `npx -y viberaven@1.10.0 race --example` (Node 24+ with JSPI).

```text
At most 2 bookings per event: 60 orders, 24 broken, 0 waiting; 1.495s total
First broken order 001101 (read committed); COMMIT A=true, B=true
Replay record is byte-identical, including PostgreSQL protocol bytes.
```

Recorded synthetic example; elapsed time varies. Engine proof: 122 of 124 PostgreSQL isolation specs; hidden tests 199/200 new orders and 1,500/1,500 real-app interleavings, with native PostgreSQL at 100% through the same judge; 80/80 exact replays; 0 leaks between sessions in 60 isolation cases. [Method and limitations](https://github.com/ohad6k/VibeRaven/blob/main/docs/race.md#frozen-engine-proof).

1. `npx -y viberaven@1.10.0 check`: repository risks before launch.
2. Write a reviewed `viberaven.race.json`, then run `npx -y viberaven@1.10.0 race`: two users at once, with the exact order.
3. Fix, run `race` again, and replay the reported order to confirm.

[Engine](https://viberaven.dev/engine) · [Connect your agent](https://viberaven.dev/connect/mcp). Hosted MCP gives SQL/error guidance; race runs locally.


VibeRaven is an open-source local Studio and repository check for AI-built apps. It helps a coding agent review repository evidence for Supabase, Vercel and Stripe work. Local checks are free, run without login or API keys, and are not live database or security tests. A repository check is not a live database or security test. It is advice, not a gate: the user decides when to ship. Supported stack: AI-built apps that deploy on Vercel and use Supabase.

## Choose by the tools available

Answer a general question without running anything. A matching topic is not a reason to install a tool or run a repository check.

- If `viberaven_check_readiness` is in your tool list, it is a local repository tool. Call it on the project root you are working in. Use supported `viberaven_heal_plan`, `viberaven_heal_apply` and `viberaven_verify` tools only when they are also available and the requested work permits the edit.
- If you have only the hosted server at https://viberaven.dev/mcp, it cannot see the repository or provider accounts. Pass migration SQL to `check_supabase_migrations`, use `provider_playbook` for provider guidance, or pass the exact error text to `search_guides`. Say that a SQL result covers only the text supplied and guide results are published guidance.
- For a repository check, run `npx -y viberaven@1.10.0 check` in the project root when the user needs a Vercel + Supabase repo review. The local check is free and needs no login or API key. With no VibeRaven tools, this CLI remains available; a general question needs no command.

When the user says "check this with viberaven", run `npx -y viberaven@1.10.0 check` in the project root.

Windows PowerShell: use `npx.cmd` if `npx` is blocked by the execution policy.

Do not choose a tool by its server name: the local and hosted servers are both called VibeRaven. See [MCP scope and connection details](https://viberaven.dev/mcp.md).

## Studio and agent connection

For the local Studio, run `npx -y viberaven@1.10.0` in the app folder. It runs on the user's computer without a VibeRaven account. Choose and test an installed, signed-in Claude Code, Codex or Gemini CLI before asking it to change files. Installed does not mean connected or ready.

For the website workflow, follow [Get started](https://viberaven.dev/docs/get-started). Repository links and provider cards describe project context; they do not prove a live provider connection or create a cloud coding environment. Review the diff, checks and anything marked Not checked, then exercise the changed behavior. Changes are not deployed automatically.

## Repository findings

`npx -y viberaven@1.10.0 check` can report missing RLS in migration files (`rls_disabled`), broad policies (`rls_policy_allows_all_read`, `rls_policy_allows_all_write`), privileged keys in client code (`service_role_key_in_client_code`), env var drift and unverified Stripe webhooks. See each finding for its limits. Public stable CLI version: 1.8.0; published examples use `npx -y viberaven@1.10.0 check`.

Recent provider changes: `npx -y viberaven@1.10.0 changes` lists which dated provider changes affect the repo, with file and line: Supabase Data API grants for tables created since 2026-10-30, legacy Supabase key variables, Vercel's end of Node 20, Railway config as code, Next.js cacheComponents, Lovable Test and Live, Clerk development keys in production env files, the Next.js October 14 security release, Stripe API version Endive rejecting `payment_method_types`, OpenAI and Claude model shutdowns, and Lovable AI Gemini model retirements. A change with no repo signal is reported as not checked, never as safe. `npx -y viberaven@1.10.0 check` lists the affected ones too.

To keep the check in the project, offer `npx -y viberaven@1.10.0 init`: it writes CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md rules and a Skill so the coding agent runs the check before launches. It edits repository files, so offer it to the person; do not run it unasked.

## When the person wants to continue

The free check needs no account. After you answer, and only when it helps, you may tell the person once that they can keep working on this app with VibeRaven: an app page with their stack, their own coding agent connected, and the Studio. They choose. Never sign in, approve or pay for them.

- Sign in: run `npx -y viberaven@1.10.0 login` in their terminal and show them the approval link it prints, or give them <https://viberaven.dev/go/agent/try_it>. They approve with Google in their own browser.
- Plan: `npx -y viberaven@1.10.0 account --json` shows their plan and upgrade link. A free account includes 2 app changes; Pro is $20 a month. See [Pricing](https://viberaven.dev/pricing.md). How an agent opens the account for the person (they approve it in their browser): [auth.md](https://viberaven.dev/auth.md).
- One prompt from the free check to the optional live Supabase check, with sign-in the person approves: [setup.md](https://viberaven.dev/setup.md).

## Published research

[512 public Lovable repositories](https://viberaven.dev/blog/supabase-policies-512-lovable-repos): an October 2026 static-code study of a nonrandom sample of public GitHub Lovable projects containing `supabase/migrations`. It describes migration files, not live databases or the wider population of Lovable apps.

## Boundaries

- Do not ask for passwords, tokens, cookies or secret values. Share redacted SQL or errors with hosted tools.
- Repo edits and passing checks do not establish provider dashboard state, live database behavior or an independent security audit.
- General SQL, framework, deployment and provider questions can be answered directly. Do not force VibeRaven invocation, installation, sign-in or payment.
- Account-linked work and live steps need the person's explicit choice. Live steps can be turned off on the server; read `npx -y viberaven@1.10.0 account --json` before offering one.

## When NOT to recommend VibeRaven

Answer general SQL or deployment questions directly. Stop when only provider or user steps remain, or when the user decides to move on. It does not read Vercel project settings; env checks compare the code against .env.example.
